LAW AND MOTION 301, RE: DEMURRER TO AMENDED COMPLAINT. NO APPEARANCE WAS MADE BY ANY PARTY, COUNSEL, OR INTERESTED PERSON. THE COURT ADOPTS ITS TENTATIVE RULING AS FOLLOWS: THE DEMURRER OR THE TRUE WIND DEFENDANTS TO THE THIRD CAUSE OF ACTION FOR DISABILITY DISCRIMINATION AND THE FOURTH CAUSE OF ACTION FOR FAILURE TO ACCOMMODATE IN THE SECOND AMENDED COMPLAINT FILED BY PLAINTIFF RENEE HESELGREN IS OVERRULED AS TO BOTH CLAIMS. SEE MINI MINUTES FOR COMPLETE RULING. COUNSEL FOR THE PREVAILING PARTY IS REQUIRED TO PREPARE AND SUBMIT TO DEPT. 301 A PROPOSED FORM OF ORDER WHICH REPEATS VERBATIM THE SUBSTANTIVE PORTION OF THE TENTATIVE RULING. JUDGE: HAROLD E. KAHN. DEMURRER to Amended COMPLAINT
Off Calendar Jul-31-2026 Text Ruling
MINI MINUTES: DEFENDANTS TRUE WIND CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, LP, TRUE WIND CAPITAL GP, LLC, TRUE WIND CAPITAL GP II, LLC, TRUE WIND CAPITAL, L.P., TRUE WIND CAPITAL II, L.P., and TRUE WIND CAPITAL II-A, L.P.'s DEMURRER to Amended COMPLAINT.

No appearance was made by any Party, Counsel, or Interested Person. The court adopts its tentative ruling as follows: The demurrer or the True Wind defendants to the third cause of action for disability discrimination and the fourth cause of action for failure to accommodate in the second amended complaint filed by plaintiff Renee Heselgren is overruled as to both claims.

Defendants' demurrer is based on Code of Civil Procedure section 430.10(e). The issue under section 430.10(e) is, taking the facts properly pleaded as true, whether the challenged cause of action necessarily fails to state a cause for relief.? (See Code Civ. Proc. Sec. 430.10(e); Blank v. Kirwan (1985) 39 Cal.3d 311, 318.) In assessing whether the complaint states a cause of action, the court accepts all properly pleaded material facts, but not contentions, deductions, or conclusions of fact or law. (Minton v. Dignity Health (2019) 39 Cal.App.5th 1155, 1161.) "[I]f, on consideration of all facts stated, it appears that plaintiff is entitled to any relief against defendant, the complaint will be held good, though facts may not be clearly stated, or may be intermingled with a statement of other facts irrelevant to cause of action shown, or though plaintiff may demand relief to which he is not entitled under facts alleged."? (Augustine v. Trucco (1954) 124 Cal.App.2d 229, 236, quoting Matteson v. Wagoner (1905) 147 Cal. 739, 742.) The court liberally construes the complaint. (Code Civ. Proc. Sec. 452.)

"A prima facie case of disability discrimination under FEHA requires the employee to show he or she (1) suffered from a disability, (2) was otherwise qualified to do his or her job, and (3) was subjected to adverse employment action because of the disability." (Nealy v. City of Santa Monica (2015) 234 Cal.App.4th 359, 378.) To establish a failure to accommodate claim, a plaintiff must show: (1) she has a disability covered by FEHA; (2) she can perform the essential functions of the position; and (3) the employer failed reasonably to accommodate the disability. (Brown v. Los Angeles Unified School District (2021) 60 Cal.App.5th 1092, 1107.) Plaintiff adequately allees claims for both disability discrimination and failure to accommodate.

The May 11, 2026 order on defendants' earlier demurrer stated that plaintiff had not sufficiently alleged her qualification "to do her job or how she was able to perform its essential functions." Plaintiff has now done so by alleging that she "was able to perform the essential functions of her job with reasonable accommodation, had a reasonable accommodation been made, including but not limited to a finite leave of absence from work." (SAC 67, 81.) While brief, the quoted language from her second amended complaint has provided the requisite information missing from the first amended complaint. If defendants desire more detail, they should seek it by discovery.

Counsel for the prevailing party is required to prepare and submit to Dept. 301 a proposed form of order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling.
